newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik talks delayed, opposition chief held up.
newsitem.headline: Tajik talks delayed, opposition chief held up.

text.p: Peace negotiations between Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri scheduled for Monday have been postponed because Nuri is stuck in the Afghan town of Kandahar, a Tajik official said.

Nuri was travelling in a United Nations aircraft on Saturday to the talks in northern Afghanistan when jets of the radical Islamic Taleban militia forced it to land. The Taleban said on Sunday the plane had been released and authorised to fly on.
"Due to Nuri's delay with the Taleban, the meeting has been postponed," Rakhmonov's spokesman, Zafar Saidov, told Reuters in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
The talks' delay was also confirmed by a spokesman for the Tajik Islamist opposition based in Dushanbe, Abdunabi Sattorzoda. "He (Nuri) is a guest of the Taleban," he said.
Both Saidov and Sattorzoda said the two leaders would try to meet in the northern Afghan town of Kunduz on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Sattorzoda, a member of a United Nations commission in Dushanbe which monitors a much flouted ceasefire, said fighting between Tajik government forces and Islamist guerrillas continued to rage around the town of Garm on Monday, around 200 km (130 miles) east of the Tajik capital.

Tens of thousands have been killed and many more made homeless in the former Soviet republic's bitter four-year civil war. Regional and clan rivalries underlie the conflict between the Islamist rebels and the secular government.
